attributes.residual: THE OPEN HALF IS NOW NAMED AND THE DECLARED-PAD AXIS IS CLOSED. Fresh measurement (both sides, every N(r1) displacement dumped from both objects, frames read off the epilogue addi r1,r1,232): the region 8..103 is 96 bytes on BOTH sides and holds 56 dead bytes on BOTH sides. TARGET: 8 param, 40 dead at 16-55, six 4-use f32 temporaries at 56/60/64/68/72/76, two s16[2] buffers at 80/82 and 84/86, 16 dead at 88-103. OURS: 8 param, six f32 temporaries and ONE s16[2] at 16-43, 4-byte align gap, stackLayout[56] at 48-103. So the 48 bytes the CB record could not explain at target 8-55 are NOT an outgoing-argument area and NOT an inlined-callee reservation: they are 8 bytes of param area plus 40 bytes of PAD. The two-buffer split reproduces the target's slot multiset EXACTLY (six 4-use f32 slots plus four 1-use s16 slots, 20 distinct slots vs the target's 20) — that half is SOLVED and reproducible. What defeats the other half: MWCC allocates its own bit-trick temporaries at the BOTTOM of the local area and a DECLARED pad cannot be pushed beneath them. Measured three independent times now (CB probe 4, and probes 1 and 2 here): with a last-declared pad, exactly four of the six f32 temporaries stay pinned at 16/20/24/28 and the pad lands ABOVE them, straddling the temporary group rather than displacing it (probe 1: pad at 40-79, temps split 16-28 + 80,84; probe 2: pad at 32-71, temps split 16-28 + 72,76). Hoisting the buffers and sx/sy to function scope moves the s16 group ABOVE the f32 group (correct target ORDER) but does not fuse the two allocation regions and does not recover the 8-byte frame overshoot. DO NOT RE-PROBE ANY DECLARED-PAD ARRANGEMENT. UNPARK CONDITION, unchanged in kind but now correctly scoped: a way to make MWCC place its expression temporaries ABOVE a declared local, or to eliminate the six memory temporaries entirely by respelling the six FloatBits and-mask operations so their results stay in registers — the latter is the genuinely untried axis and is the recommended next lane.
